title: When Does Fine-Tuning Beat Prompting for Qiskit-to-CUDA-Q Translation? An Execution-Verified Study
abstract: arXiv:2611.29793v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Moving quantum code from Qiskit to NVIDIA CUDA-Q is a practical adoption cost that language models are starting to automate. We ask whether a small open model can learn this translation, and how to measure it so that the result can be trusted. Both programs can be executed and their state vectors compared, so a kernel counts as correct only if it prepares the same state as the Qiskit reference (fidelity >= 0.999), with no text matching and no LLM judge. We build a 640-task benchmark with three test sets (larger circuits, an unseen circuit family, an unseen Qiskit coding style) and a QuantumKatas regression probe, and we test the evaluator before training. Measurement counts miss every phase-only error; a surface rule-based translator solves two of three original splits (text substitution); a converter that executes the Qiskit input and maps the circuit solves all 640 tasks -- so the benchmark measures source-level translation, not whet

translated_title: 微调何时胜过提示工程实现 Qiskit 到 CUDA-Q 的翻译？一项经执行验证的研究
translated_abstract: arXiv:2611.29793v1 公告类型： cross 摘要： 将量子代码从 Qiskit 迁移到 NVIDIA CUDA-Q 是一种实际采用中的成本，语言模型正开始将这一过程自动化。我们探究一个小型开源模型能否学会这种翻译，以及应如何度量它才能使结果可信。由于两个程序都可以被执行并比较其状态向量，因此只有当生成的内核制备出与 Qiskit 参考相同的状态（保真度 >= 0.999）时才被判定为正确——不使用文本匹配，也不使用 LLM 评判。我们构建了一个包含 640 个任务的基准，其中包括三个测试集（更大的电路、未见过的电路族、未见过的 Qiskit 编码风格）以及一个 QuantumKatas 回归探针，并在训练之前对评估器进行了测试。基于测量计数的方法会漏掉所有纯相位误差；一个基于规则的表面翻译器解决了三个原始划分中的两个（文本替换）；而一个执行 Qiskit 输入并映射电路的转换器解决了全部 640 个任务——因此该基准衡量的是源级翻译，而非……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究提出了一个以执行结果验证正确性（基于状态向量保真度而非文本匹配或LLM评判）的640任务基准，用于评估Qiskit到CUDA-Q的量子代码翻译，并通过预训练的基线测试确保基准真正衡量源级翻译能力而非表面规则替换。
en_tdlr: This study introduces an execution-verified 640-task benchmark for Qiskit-to-CUDA-Q translation, where correctness is determined by state-vector fidelity comparison (>= 0.999) rather than text matching, with pre-training baseline tests showing the benchmark measures genuine source-level translation rather than surface-level rule substitution.
